title: Performance standup slate 2026-09-14
content:
Quick summary:
- Short sync to capture a new tail-latency/throughput correlation observed in the last 48h shadow runs. Not a full incident postmortem but a working hypothesis list and short experiments to run this week.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (owner)
- Jonas Patel
- Priya Singh
- Luca Bernal
- Quick RT from SRE: K. Osei (joined for infra notes)

Observed signal (what changed):
- On 2026-09-12 22:00 UTC we started seeing intermittent p99 spikes (~700ms -> 1.4s) for the small-text chat profile while aggregate QPS stayed ~flat (~450 qps). Throughput measured in tokens/s dropped by ~8% during spike windows.
- The p95 remained relatively stable; the tail (p99/p999) was the primary regressor.
- Spike windows were short (10–60s) and often coincided with a small increase in request size variance (more long-context requests).

Quick diagnostics we ran during the meeting:
1) Trace sampling (100 traces from a symptomatic window):
   - Many traces show a host-level stall in the "KVCache lookup" span and occasional serialization of requests at the server gRPC worker queue.
   - GPU utilization stayed high but steady (~85-92%); no obvious OOM or CUDA resets in that window.
2) Node telemetry cross-check:
   - PCIe retransmit counters on two nodes increased during spikes (Luca), suggesting transient PCIe/driver noise.
   - NUMA local/remote memory ratio drifted on the same nodes when we primed large-context requests (Priya).
3) Client-side logs:
   - A small fraction of clients were sending bursty parallel requests framed as many short streams instead of a single multiplexed stream. This correlated with the worst tails.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1 (high confidence): NUMA imbalance + driver-level PCIe retries during intermittent long-context requests causes stalls in memory reads for KV cache, raising per-request latency and backpressureing request queues -> p99 spikes.
- H2 (medium confidence): gRPC worker queue starvation from client-side burst patterns interacts badly with our batching heuristic when sudden variability in sequence length occurs.
- H3 (low confidence): Rare scheduler preemption pattern in host kernel causing microstalls on the inference thread (we saw hints but not strong evidence).

Mini experiments planned (order matters):
- E1 (run immediately, low risk): Force NUMA-local allocation for KV-cache memory on a 3-node canary pool and re-run the 1-hour shadow workload used yesterday. Measure p99/p999, PCIe counters. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-09-16.
- E2 (parallel to E1): Temporarily enable a conservative batching cap for the chat-small profile (reduce max batch size by 20%) on a subset of traffic to check for improvement on p99 without hurting throughput. Owner: Jonas. ETA: 2026-09-15.
- E3 (instrumentation run): Increase trace sampling rate for KVCache read latency and add a lightweight counter for PCIe retry events via eBPF probe on suspect nodes. Owner: Luca + SRE K. Osei. ETA: 2026-09-17.
- E4 (client-side mitigation test): Roll out a short-lived client guideline via SDK to prefer multiplexed streams for parallel prompt calls; Shadow clients only. Owner: Maya + DevEx. ETA: 2026-09-20.

Immediate action items from meeting (concrete):
- Priya: Prepare NUMA-localization canary image and test on staging cluster; record before/after PCIe counters. (due 2026-09-16)
- Jonas: Deploy conservative batching cap on 10% of traffic; create dashboard showing p50/p95/p99 and tokens/s pre/post. (due 2026-09-15)
- Luca: Wire eBPF trace for PCIe retry counts and KV read latencies into Perf dashboards; short-lived retention. (due 2026-09-17)
- Maya: Draft a short internal note for SDK guidance on stream multiplexing and coordinate a shadow rollout. (due 2026-09-18)
- K. Osei (SRE): Reserve 3 nodes with identical kernel/driver versions for canary tests and audit driver changelogs for the last 30 days. (due 2026-09-15)

Metrics to capture during experiments (minimum):
- p50/p95/p99/p999 latency (endpoint-level, and per-host tail breakdown)
- tokens/s (aggregate and per-host)
- batch size distribution pre/post tweak
- PCIe retry/transmit counters per NIC/GPU link
- NUMA local/remote allocations ratio for KV cache memory

Fallback criteria (stop test and roll back):
- Token throughput drops by >10% sustained for >5 minutes OR
- p99 increases by >2x relative to baseline for >3 minutes OR
- Any node shows a kernel oops or GPU driver CTA reset

Notes / context and linkage to prior work:
- This feels adjacent to the "kv-cache-regression-hypothesis-worklog-2025-07-22" thread, but different vector (driver/NUMA vs algorithmic KV eviction).
- Related PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/2891 (instrumentation changes merged last month).
- We observed a similar but rarer pattern in Jan 2026 when a driver bump coincided with heavy long-context traffic; that run had noisy PCIe counters but we lacked eBPF traces.

Discussion points deferred to follow-up:
- Whether to enforce NUMA pinning by default for all dedicated pools (tradeoff: slightly higher memory fragmentation vs tail reduction).
- Long-term: revisit batching heuristic to be sequence-length-aware, not only queue-size aware.

Next sync: 2026-09-18 09:30 PT, quick 20m check-in to review E1/E2 initial findings.

Appendix (short run snapshot):
- Baseline (2026-09-12 20:00–22:00 UTC): p99=710ms, p95=180ms, tokens/s=6200
- Symptomatic window sample (2026-09-12 22:07–22:08 UTC): p99=1.42s, p95=190ms, tokens/s=5700, PCIe-retry-events on node-7: +320 (vs baseline +12)
- Quick grep: no CUDA errors, no OOM in dmesg; kernel logs show 3 "link retry" events for PCIe on node-7 during that minute.

Notes to self: capture full raw trace archive and attach to the confluence follow-up page for the postmortem if E1/E2 don't resolve.

End of notes.
